To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stepwise ligand transformation of a porphine molecule adsorbed onto the Au(111) surface proceeds via a concentrical electrocyclic ring opening, with the final transformation product being the tetrabenzoporphyrazine.

we have studied the stepwise transformation of the organic molecule iron octaethyl porphyrin (OEP) to iron tetrabensoporphyrin (TBP) on Au(111), and observed the change in the magnetic fingerprint of the molecule during the transformation.
the magnetic coupling of an Fe(II)-porphyrin molecule on a Au(111) surface can be controlled by a stepwise intramolecular ligation reaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the investigation of the surface-assisted intracellular ligand reaction of iron porphyrin molecules adsorbed on a Au(111) single-crystal substrate, which is studied with scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS).
the development of new methods for the characterization of single molecules on surfaces and the study of chemical reactions on metal surfaces.
the development of a new class of molecular magnets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ligand transformation is a surface-assisted intraligand reaction, which is driven by the substrate temperature and the adsorbate-adsorbate interaction.
the magnetic fingerprint of a molecule can change by a surface-assisted intrasurface reaction, and that the change is due to a change in the magnetic coupling with the substrate.
the ligand reaction is not only a surface-induced process, but also a surface-assisted process, as the reaction is initiated by the surface and the product is stabilized by the surface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can change the electronic and spin properties of a single molecule on a surface, by a chemical reaction, and that we are able to follow this reaction stepwise with STM.
we can use STM to monitor the transformation of a porphin molecule on Au(111).
a single porphyrin adsorbed on a gold surface is able to undergo a stepwise ligation reaction to form a tetrabenzoporphyin molecule.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a metal-organic molecule adsorbed at a metal surface can be used to study the interplay between the molecule's electronic structure and the substrate.
the substrate plays an active role in the reaction and the resulting product is a function of the substrate.
the ligand reaction can be used as an additional degree of freedom to control the coupling of the molecule with the surface.
